t: You're on Thurloe Place, a street in Kensington and Chelsea. It is named after John Thurloe, a seventeenth-century English barrister from Great Milton in Oxfordshire, and a member of Lincoln's Inn. Thurloe served as secretary to the council of state during the Protectorate and acted as spymaster for Oliver Cromwell. He was also Postmaster General between 1655 and 1660.
